jobs.description:
We are looking for a Software Engineer who wants to build and ship new features that quickly reach customers, on top of an engine that already runs at scale. You join our platform team, which owns several live domains that our customers depend on every day. The foundations are solid and well maintained, so your time goes into new use cases and features rather than firefighting. Whether you have a couple of years of experience or a few more, we would like to see your application.

**What's in it for you?

**

• Hear directly from the people using what you build. Customer feedback feeds straight back into the roadmap, and you work on features and product decisions that matter to end users.

• Build on a system with real scale behind it. The event system spans 8 domains, exposes 20+ event types as webhooks, and powers 10 configurable alert types for our end users - currently ~20k active configurations triggering ~200k events every weekday. The team owns 8+ public APIs end to end, crucial for customers' day-to-day business.

• Learn from experts who share. You’ll join a talkative team of experienced domain experts who love discussing technical topics.

• Grow with support. Scoped, well-defined assignments to start, senior colleagues pairing and reviewing your work, and shared ownership of keeping things running.

• See your work ship. We favour small, frequent releases over long project cycles, so what you build lands in production fast.

**Who are you ideally?

**You are a backend developer with strong Java skills who is at home on live production systems.

• Hands-on experience with Java, Spring Boot, Kafka, and REST APIs, in particular building and running your own services in a modern cloud-based microservice and event-driven architecture.

• You are comfortable working on live production systems with high data volumes and migration paths, keeping quality, observability, reliability, and performance in mind.

• You enjoy talking tech: you like discussing technical topics widely, learning, and listening in on topics not always directly related to your own tasks.

• You are motivated by incremental, high-quality delivery on products that are already live, bringing a fresh perspective that helps rework existing infrastructure where it is holding us back, and you treat the tools already in our platform as solid building blocks.

• Nice to have: Flink and stateful processing (or the willingness to learn it, since it is widely used here), relational databases, and Grafana and Prometheus, our “bread and butter”.

You embrace AI as part of how you engineer. From prototyping through to production, you use AI tools as an integrated part of your workflow, not as a shortcut but as a force multiplier. That said, this isn't the main thing we're hiring for: curiosity and a willingness to use it well matter more than deep prior experience.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries, this is what we're looking for ideally. If you're excited about this role but your background doesn't align perfectly with every point above, we encourage you to apply.

**Primary Responsibilities

**

• Improve, extend and run the live domains our team owns, including telemetry storage and APIs, the event system, and the alerting engine, without disrupting production.

• Build and run your own services, with migration paths when architecture or data formats need to change.

• Work closely with the internal teams building products on top of the platform you help shape.

• Keep the platform reliable and observable at high data volumes.

****Our hiring process

****Don’t waste your time writing the perfect cover letter. We want you to create an impact that matters - and that’s not in the cover letter.

• Initial phone conversation with a colleague from our P&T team.

• Virtual meet and greet with your potential new leader and someone from the team, so you’ll get to know the role and team better.

• Assignment-specific interview with the hiring manager and a lead engineer from the team. We want to give you a real insight into the work. You’ll receive a case to prepare ahead of the interview and present to relevant colleagues - people you’ll also work closely with in the role.

• If needed, we will obtain references from former employers and conduct background checks at relevant levels.

• Offer presentation and walk-through.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We’re committed to construction - one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products - it’s a way of life at Trackunit. We’re proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues come together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

The question is: Are you in?

You’ll help shape the systems that keep a leading energy trading business accurate and compliant, while giving us the capacity to modernise our solutions and build what comes next.

Here’s what the job entails

In the role, your primary function will be to design, build and improve C# solutions for what happens after an energy trade is captured: settlement, invoicing and regulatory reporting. As an experienced engineer, you will take ownership of solutions from ideas to production while helping make knowledge and ownership more distributed across the team. You will gain valuable insight into energy trading and financial regulation, while working with modern engineering approaches such as event-driven architecture and AI-assisted development.

More specifically, your responsibilities include:

• designing, developing and maintaining C# services that turn every energy trade we make into correct accurate invoices, settlements and regulatory reports

• taking ownership of your solutions from idea to production, spotting and addressing issues early before they affect the business

• analysing how our current systems and data work, and simplifying complex or ageing solutions to make them easier to run, understand and change

• working closely with the product manager, product owner and solution architect to turn business needs, including regulatory rules, into well-tested and well-documented solutions

• sharing your knowledge through code reviews, documentation and mentoring, helping build shared knowledge and ownership across the team

Meet your team

You will join our Late Trade Flow team, where we work with the systems that handle trades after they are made. Our primary responsibility is making sure these processes are accurate, timely and compliant with regulation. An important focus for the team is modernising these solutions and building the foundation for the next stage of the business, increasingly using event-driven architecture and AI.

We are a team of software and data engineers, supported by a product manager, product owner and solution architect, working side by side with our finance and trading colleagues. We value ownership, openness and learning from each other, and we actively share knowledge through collaboration, mentoring and feedback. As a curious and proactive team, we continuously explore how new technology and better ways of working can improve the solutions we build.

But enough about us… over to you!

As you will be working with business-critical solutions, we imagine that you enjoy taking ownership and following your work from idea to production. You take a proactive approach to challenges, spotting issues and opportunities early and acting on them. At the same time, you enjoy working closely with others, sharing your knowledge and learning from the people around you.

Furthermore, we imagine that you:

• have solid professional experience developing production software in C# and .NET

• have practical experience with domain-driven design and event-driven architecture

• bring an analytical approach to problem solving, including working with data and complex business rules

• have experience working in agile teams and contributing to product development

Help us evolve the technical foundation for digital manufacturing at VELUX. As IIoT Platform Technical Lead, you will lead the technical direction of our shared IIoT platform while taking part in engineering. You will enable development teams to build manufacturing applications through reliable connectivity, standardised shop floor data and reusable platform services.

Meet your future team

You will join the Industrial IoT Platform Team, part of IT & Digital Enablement. The team develops and maintains the shared IIoT platform that supports manufacturing applications through connectivity, data and reusable technical capabilities.

As IIoT Platform Technical Lead, you will provide day-to-day technical leadership across the engineering group. Working closely with senior IIoT platform engineers, architects, vendors and manufacturing stakeholders, you will coordinate decisions, coach engineers and help move delivery forward. The role has no formal people-management responsibility.

What We Offer

This role combines contributing to the shared IIoT platform’s technical direction with direct engineering work. You will lead day-to-day technical direction and engineering execution, contributing to design, development, testing, reviews and complex problem-solving. You will turn product priorities into a coherent platform roadmap, engineering practices and clear guardrails.

You will balance a clear technical direction with close collaboration, involving the team in technical decisions and finding practical compromises that support both platform integrity and delivery needs.

The goal in this role means a clear and maintained platform roadmap, faster onboarding and greater reuse, improved visibility of platform health, and well-defined ownership between shared platform capabilities and domain-specific application logic.

More specifically your tasks will be to:

• Own and maintain the IIoT platform technical roadmap, including runtime, frameworks, connectivity components, data contracts, developer tooling, observability and lifecycle enablers. Provide estimates, sequencing, dependency and risk input and coordinate with dependent product teams.

• Coordinate technical planning, reviews and coaching across the platform engineering group, aligning key design decisions with senior IIoT platform engineers. Act as the first technical escalation point. Guide external engineering contributions so standards, knowledge and lifecycle accountability remain within the team. Escalate material architecture and cross-platform decisions through the appropriate technical governance.

• Contribute hands-on to platform services and reusable components through design, development, testing and improvement. Focus your direct contribution where technical depth, complex problem-solving or delivery needs require it.

• Support platform observability, technical investigations and follow-through on incidents, problems and improvement actions in collaboration with the Operations Manager.

• Manage platform lifecycle health, including security, patching, vulnerability remediation, upgrades, documentation, supportability, and technical debt.

The role can be based in Skjern, Østbirk, Kolding or Hørsholm. Regular on-site presence in Skjern and at manufacturing locations in Denmark is required, along with occasional international travel. When tasks and projects allow, you may work from home up to two days per week.

What You Will Bring Into The Organization

You bring 7+ years of relevant experience in software, platform or integration engineering, including technical leadership in an industrial IT/OT or digital manufacturing environment. You understand both manufacturing-domain needs and Unified Namespace. You use that understanding to make technical choices that work for platform users and the engineering team.

Moreover, we expect that you:

• Bring practical knowledge across industrial connectivity and edge technologies, including MQTT, edge runtimes and container orchestration. You also understand industrial data contracts, observability or SRE practices, and OT cyber security.

• Can translate product priorities into an actionable platform roadmap, technical guardrails and engineering practices.

• Can make practical technical design decisions while involving engineers and relevant stakeholders in finding workable solutions.

• Use effective coaching, facilitation, collaboration and communication skills across engineers, product roles, architects, vendors and manufacturing stakeholders.

• Apply a platform mindset focused on reuse, self-service, consumer enablement, operational excellence and long-term maintainability.

Ready to apply?

Learn more about the VELUX Group online at www.velux.com where you can read more about working at our company and what to expect of our recruitment process.

About MITS Industries

MITS Industries is establishing an R&D and design site in Copenhagen focused on advanced RF systems, signal intelligence, aerospace technologies, and mission-critical product development.

The site will build core engineering capabilities in RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, RF testing and characterization, rugged mechanical integration, and the industrialization of complex radio-electronic systems.

The Copenhagen team will work closely with strategic partners and engineering teams across Europe, playing a leading role in the development, validation, and industrialization of advanced technologies for defense, aerospace, and other demanding applications.

One of the initial focus areas will be the development of an advanced aerospace signal intelligence product platform. The work will cover RF and system architecture, antenna system design, signal acquisition, embedded control, laboratory validation, mechanical integration, integration with the satellite platform, and preparation for production and field deployment.

The ambition is to build a strong technical design site capable of taking complex RF products, modules, and platforms from architecture and detailed design through prototyping, testing, validation, industrialization, and deployment.

About the role

MITS Industries is looking for a Senior Systems Engineer, RF Systems to join the core Copenhagen R&D team and help build the site’s systems engineering capability for advanced RF, aerospace, and signal-intelligence products. You will translate product, mission, and stakeholder needs into clear functional, performance, and parametric requirements, system architectures, subsystem allocation, interface definitions, integration strategies, and verification plans. The work covers requirements decomposition and traceability, system performance budgeting, interface management, technical risk analysis, design reviews, integration planning, and system level verification and validation. You will work closely with RF and microwave hardware engineers, antenna systems engineers, embedded and control engineers, signal-processing engineers, RF test and characterization engineers, mechanical design engineers, project managers, and partner engineering teams. You will ensure that requirements, design decisions, implementation, integration, testing, and validation remain connected throughout the development lifecycle. The role requires strong RF system understanding, structured systems-engineering expertise, technical ownership, and a hands-on integration mindset. Working with technical leadership, you will turn product and architectural intent into an executable, traceable, and verifiable engineering baseline and help carry the product through integration, qualification, and deployment.

Key responsibilities

• Translate product, mission, and stakeholder needs into clear functional, performance, parametric, interface, environmental, and verification requirements.

• Develop and maintain the functional and physical system architecture, allocate requirements to subsystems, and define key technical trade-offs.

• Establish and maintain system performance budgets and constraints covering RF performance, timing and synchronization, data flow, power, thermal performance, mass, and platform interfaces.

• Define and maintain system requirements, subsystem requirements, interface control documentation, acceptance criteria, and verification logic.

• Align RF subsystem requirements, including frequency coverage, sensitivity, selectivity, dynamic range, noise figure, linearity, phase noise, spurious responses, channel isolation, and interference resilience.

• Define antenna-system requirements covering frequency coverage, antenna gain, polarization, radiation-pattern characteristics, isolation between antenna channels, placement, and platform integration.

• Define embedded control, data acquisition, timing, synchronization, diagnostics, logging, networking, and system-monitoring requirements.

• Coordinate mechanical and platform requirements covering dimensions, mass, thermal management, connectors, cabling, grounding, shielding, mounting, environmental constraints, and serviceability.

• Work with RF test and characterization engineers to define measurable acceptance criteria, calibration needs, verification methods, test coverage, and required evidence.

• Prepare and maintain system requirements specifications, interface-control documents, system budgets, integration plans, verification plans, compliance matrices, and technical decision records.

• Lead system integration planning and support prototype bring-up, laboratory validation, qualification, and field-test preparation.

• Identify system-level risks, interface conflicts, missing requirements, invalid assumptions, and integration blockers, and drive their resolution.

• Facilitate cross-functional technical alignment between engineering disciplines, technical leadership, manufacturing partners, and partner engineering teams.

• Support requirements reviews, system design reviews, integration reviews, test readiness reviews, and milestone decisions.

• Maintain traceability between stakeholder needs, requirements, design decisions, implementation, verification results, and acceptance evidence.

• Help establish systems-engineering methods, documentation practices, requirements-management workflows, and technical-review processes for future MITS Industries development programs.

Required qualifications and experience

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in electrical or electronic engineering, telecommunications, systems engineering, aerospace engineering, applied physics, or a related field.

• 6+ years of professional experience in systems engineering for complex RF, electronic, aerospace, or other mission-critical systems.

• Strong understanding of RF systems, including receiver architectures, RF signal paths, antenna interfaces, signal acquisition, data conversion, embedded control, timing and synchronization, calibration, and system validation.

• Proven experience translating product, mission, and stakeholder needs into functional, performance, parametric, interface, environmental, and verification requirements.

• Experience developing functional and physical system architectures, decomposing systems into subsystems, allocating requirements, and defining interfaces and technical trade-offs.

• Experience establishing and maintaining system performance budgets and constraints covering RF performance, timing and synchronization, data flow, power, thermal performance, mass, and platform interfaces.

• Strong understanding of requirements decomposition, traceability, acceptance criteria, and verification methods, including analysis, inspection, demonstration, and testing.

• Experience preparing and maintaining system requirements specifications, interface-control documents, integration plans, verification plans, compliance matrices, and technical decision records.

• Practical experience with requirements-management and traceability tools such as IBM Engineering DOORS, Jama Connect, Polarion, or equivalent.

• Experience working with cross-functional engineering teams covering RF and microwave hardware, antennas, embedded systems, signal processing, mechanical design, test, manufacturing, and system integration.

• Ability to evaluate technical trade-offs across RF performance, embedded implementation, mechanical and thermal constraints, testability, manufacturability, reliability, and operational use.

• Hands-on experience with prototype integration, laboratory validation, system-level debugging, and troubleshooting of complex multidisciplinary systems.

• Experience identifying and managing system-level risks, interface conflicts, assumptions, technical dependencies, and integration blockers. Strong technical communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to align senior engineers and drive decisions across engineering disciplines.

Nice to have

• Experience with signal-intelligence, direction-finding, spectrum-monitoring, or radio-surveillance systems.

• Experience with SDR-based systems and high-throughput RF data acquisition.

• Experience with broadband, multiband, coherent, or multichannel receiver systems.

• Experience with Model-Based Systems Engineering, SysML, and tools such as Cameo Systems Modeler, Enterprise Architect, or equivalent.

• Experience establishing and maintaining controlled system baselines, including requirements, interfaces, verification status, configuration, and engineering changes.

• Experience with engineering analysis, data processing, or system modelling using MATLAB, Python, or equivalent.

• Experience with field integration, testing, calibration, and deployment of complex RF or aerospace systems.

• Experience working on aerospace, mission-critical, ruggedized, or internationally distributed engineering programs.

Success in the first 6 months

• Establish the initial system requirements baseline, subsystem allocation, interface definitions, and performance budgets for the assigned product scope.

• Create a clear technical decomposition across RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, embedded control, signal processing, mechanical design, test, and system integration.

• Define the integration, verification, and validation approach for the initial prototype or subsystem, including acceptance criteria, traceability, and required evidence.

• Identify unclear interfaces, missing requirements, technical assumptions, and system-level risks early, and drive practical resolution actions. Support prototype integration, bring-up, and laboratory validation with structured system-level analysis, troubleshooting, and verification evidence.

• Establish repeatable systems-engineering practices, documentation templates, requirements-management workflows, and technical-review processes for future development programs.

jobs.description:
Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, is looking for a full-time Data manager to work at the Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Futures (Land-CRAFT).

Land-CRAFT addresses three of our major societal challenges - food security, climate change, and loss of biodiversity. With Center partners from University of Copenhagen, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (Germany), and Colorado State University (USA), we bring together expertise in climate impact research, landscape analyses, biogeochemistry, agronomy, biology, and geography to develop solution – oriented research that extends across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Established in June 2022, Land-CRAFT has built a dynamic team to undertake both fundamental and applied research aimed to reduce the environmental impact of agricultural systems, specifically regarding greenhouse gas emissions. To reach our goals, we are using a combination of empirical, field-based approaches, digital technologies, including modelling and remote sensing, while closely interacting with stakeholders. The position we advertise here is aimed at supporting these activities with respect to data management. The new employee will become part of a support team with complementary skills and work collaboratively in an active and international research environment with diverse projects and people across Department of Agroecology.

The position is available from 1st March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The duration of the position is 3 years.

Responsibilities and tasks
Your main role as part of the support team at Land-CRAFT will be to support research activities of the staff and research students (at BSc, MSc, and PhD levels) in data management, analysis and statistics. This will include maintaining and supplementing relational databases used for process-based modelling and geospatial data analyses. Main responsibilities and tasks include:

• 
Organize, archive, and document data collected by the Land-CRAFT team, including with appropriate metadata protocols

• 
Manage data transfer/sharing among Center partners and external collaborators following FAIR data principles, AU rules and regulations, and GDPR rules

• 
Manage user access and permissions within the AU File system and user data on a computational server

• 
Create and manage a database on research outputs from the Center, including e.g., publications, citations and other reports, to facilitate website updates, annual reports, and other communication platforms, as well as managing the Zenodo community

• 
Support staff and students with statistical and geospatial analyses (e.g. in R and Python)

• 
Support/manage data collection pipeline from instruments in the lab & field (including visualisation of data in e.g. Origin)

• 
Establish, maintain, and refine documentation regarding all data-related protocols (e.g. data policy, data management plans, etc.)

• 
Coordinating data management across the Department of Agroecology (about 20 % of time) in collaboration with the department’s data steward

Your profile
As a member of the Land-Craft support team, we expect you to plan and perform your tasks independently and initiate frequent feedback and communication with Land CRAFT researchers and students. The position requires that you can communicate with and support students and scientists from BSc to Professor levels, including attention to detail and quality (QA/QC) and an affinity for knowledge-sharing, e.g., in working with students as they learn to manage their own data. You have a high proficiency in English, are culturally sensitive, and can work in a large group of diverse colleagues and students. At Land-CRAFT we emphasize good relationships among colleagues and students. It is therefore important that you have a positive and open personality, stay engaged with emerging challenges and opportunities, and are ready to support colleagues when needed.

Qualifications

• 
MSc in data science, agroecology, geoscience, biology, ecology, environmental science, mathematics, geography (or related fields)

• 
Knowledge and understanding of data management plans, metadata systems, archiving practices

• 
Experience in statistical analysis; knowledge of R or Python, as well as visualisation platforms

• 
Good collaboration and communications skills across different groups of employees,

• 
High level of English proficiency and cultural sensitivity

• 
Interest in and willingness to acquire general knowledge about Land-CRAFT’s research areas

• 
Familiarity with the Danish administrative structures or Danish language.

Workplace
The place of work is Aarhus University, Ole Worms Alle 3, DK-8000 Aarhus C. The affiliation will be with the Department of Agroecology.

Who we are
At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 350 highly skilled employees, of which approximately 50% are scientific staff. More information can be found here.
We believe in encouraging inclusion, acceptance, and understanding by employing staff who bring unique perspectives to our department.

What we offer

• 
A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.

• 
An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.

• 
A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.

• 
An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.

• 
An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.

• 
Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme

Contact information
More information can be obtained from Klaus Butterbach-Bahl (klaus.butterbach bahl@agro.au.dk).

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions..You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8.

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. Stay close to the code. Lead a development team. Help shape how we build software at Dalux.

Dalux is growing, and we are looking for experienced software developers who want to combine hands-on engineering with technical leadership.

You will have significant influence on both the products we build and how we build them – including how we use agentic AI across software development.

Your role

Each Dalux development team owns one or more areas of our product portfolio, including its functionality, architecture, quality, performance, reliability, and long-term technical health.

As Team Lead, you are the technical anchor of the team. You work closely with developers, a Product Manager, and a Product Designer to understand problems, set technical direction, and turn product priorities into high-quality software.

This is primarily a technical leadership role rather than a traditional people-management position, and you will spend approximately 50% of your time developing software hands-on.

The rest of your role typically includes:

• Setting technical direction and defining architectural solutions with the team

• Working with the Product Manager to understand requirements, challenge scope, and translate priorities into development work

• Planning and prioritizing work while maintaining a healthy and sustainable flow

• Helping the team break down complex technical and product problems

• Mentoring developers through technical sparring, reviews, and day-to-day collaboration

• Taking responsibility for the quality and long-term health of your team's software

• Identifying opportunities to improve architecture, tools, development practices, and ways of working

• Driving improvements beyond your own team when they can make Dalux Development better

We expect Team Leads to have opinions, challenge existing approaches, and create clarity when there is no obvious answer.

Leading development with agentic AI

We are significantly increasing our use of agentic AI in software development.

We use and explore AI across the development lifecycle – from understanding problems and navigating codebases to implementation, testing, debugging, refactoring, and review.

As a Team Lead, you are expected to have hands-on experience using agentic AI in your own development workflow. The specific tools matter less than how you use them: providing the right context and direction, critically evaluating the output, and knowing when to intervene or take a different approach.

Your role goes beyond your own workflow. You will help your team experiment with agentic development, identify where it genuinely improves engineering effectiveness, share useful practices, and maintain the engineering judgment and quality standards required for production software.

AI can increase what capable developers can achieve, but responsibility for architecture, correctness, maintainability, and quality remains with the team.

Technologies we work with

Our platform is built on a distributed cloud architecture using AWS.

Depending on the team, you may work with technologies such as:

• Full-stack: C# / .NET, Angular / TypeScript, GitHub Copilot, MSSQL, Elasticsearch, WebGL, DirectX

• Mobile: .NET MAUI, Vulkan

• AI and Computer Vision: C++, Python, computer vision and machine learning technologies

Which team you lead depends on your technical background, interests, leadership experience, and where we see the strongest match.

Product development at Dalux

Our developers do more than implement specifications.

Developers, Product Managers, and Product Designers work together to understand problems and find solutions that balance user value, usability, technical feasibility, business viability, and long-term technical health.

As Team Lead, you bring the technical perspective into those discussions. You help the team understand why we are building something, challenge proposed solutions when necessary, and ensure technical considerations are part of product decisions from the beginning.

Your background

You are an experienced software developer who enjoys taking responsibility beyond your own code.

You may already be a Team Lead or Lead Developer. Or you may be the developer others turn to when a difficult technical decision needs to be made, a problem needs structure, or another developer needs help moving forward.

We expect that you:

• Have solid professional software development experience

• Have at least six months of practical experience using agentic AI as part of your software development workflow

• Have an educational background in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related technical field

• Have experience taking a key technical role within a development team

• Are comfortable making and facilitating technical decisions

• Enjoy mentoring and helping other developers improve

• Can create structure and direction without controlling every detail

• Have strong communication, facilitation, and planning skills

• Care about maintainability, reliability, performance, and engineering quality

• Understand how to balance short-term delivery with long-term technical health

• Can identify opportunities to improve development practices and ways of working

Experience with our exact technology stack is useful, but technical judgment, leadership ability, and strong software engineering fundamentals matter more.

What You Can Expect From Dalux

Dalux is a software company at heart, and software development is central to how we create value.

As a Team Lead, you can expect:

• Hands-on engineering – leadership does not mean leaving software development behind

• Real technical influence – short paths between ideas, discussions, and decisions

• Meaningful team ownership – teams own both product functionality and the technology behind it

• Strong technical colleagues – daily sparring with developers who care about what they build

• Close product collaboration – developers work directly with Product Managers and Product Designers

• Room to improve how we work – Team Leads are expected to challenge and evolve our development practices

• An environment actively investing in agentic AI – with the opportunity to shape how your team works with it

• High levels of trust and freedom in how you and your team solve problems

All Dalux software development takes place in-house at our headquarters in Vibenshuset, Copenhagen.

We believe working together in person makes technical collaboration, mentoring, knowledge sharing, and fast decision-making significantly easier.

About Dalux

Dalux is a Danish software company founded in 2005 by Bent Dalgaard and Torben Dalgaard.

Our core technology is developed entirely in-house, giving our developers and technical leaders the opportunity to influence both the products and the technology behind them.

Ready to lead from within the team?

If agentic AI is already part of how you develop software, tell us how you use it – and how you think a development team can use it effectively without compromising engineering quality.

Are you interested in a career in AI for materials and in accelerating the green transition? If so, we have a number of positions at DTU that might just right for you. 

The four PhD positions at DTU Energy are part of BRIGHT's mission-oriented Novel Biomanufacturing-Enabled Materials research programme, referred to as Mission 1A, which aims to create new classes of PFAS-free functional biomaterials through biotechnology. The mission's current focus are proteinaceous materials with defined composition, programmable chemistry and controlled assembly as sustainable alternatives to persistent fluorinated materials. The scientific scope spans AI-guided protein and peptide design, microbial engineering, non-canonical amino acid biosynthesis and incorporation, cell-free prototyping, fermentation, purification, materials processing, analytical quality control and structure-function characterization. The programme focuses on building an integrated pipeline from molecular design to scalable biomanufacturing and material testing, with explicit attention to manufacturability, cost, sustainability and industrial translation. Batteries provide the first proof-of-concept application, because PFAS-containing materials are currently used in several battery components and because this sector imposes strict requirements for stability, processability and performance. The broader ambition is to establish a versatile biomanufacturing platform for advanced PFAS-free materials with future relevance across energy technologies, coatings, electronics and other high-value applications.

You will work closely with experimental and computational colleagues in BRIGHT and in DTU Energy, as well as with our international collaborators, e.g., on the use cases on advanced battery materials in MaterialsCommons for Europe and on the development of Self-driving Laboratories (SDLs) at the Pioneer Center CAPeX. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
All four positions are centered on the application of novel PFAS-free proteins and polypeptides for applications in sustainable batteries. The design space for finding optimal compositions and synthesis conditions for such polymers for use as, e.g., electrolytes, binders and additives is vast, we are combining self-driving labs, high-throughput machine learning simulations, and agentic AI to transition to digitalization-based autonomous development of high-performing PFAS-free polymer materials for high-performant batteries, i.e., high electrochemical stability, ionic conductivity, coulombic efficiency, and cyclability at a low cost. The positions will target for areas specifically

• Development of automated setup for high-throughput testing of solid polymer electrolytes and binders, e.g., chemical and electrochemical stability, preparation and film casting. 
• Development of automated setup for in situ polymerization of sodium/sodium-based based battery materials
• Self-driving lab modules for autonomous testing of mechanical properties of polymer-based battery materials, interfaces and layers
• Self-driving lab modules for assembly and testing of advanced (e.g., solid-state and anode-less, sodium-based button and coin cell batteries.
Qualifications:

• Good working knowledge of electrochemistry.
• Ability to work independently and plan and carry out complicated tasks.
• Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken.
• A proactive approach to problem-solving, capable of identifying new directions and opportunities within the project.
Desirable Qualifications:

• Experience with self-driving laboratories or building custom experimental hardware

Application procedure

About BRIGHT – The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). The goal is to develop and scale innovative biosolutions within these areas, ultimately creating sustainable and competitive alternatives to fossil-based products and processes that can make significant contributions to reducing global greenhouse gas emissions.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Experimental Quantum Nanophotonics
jobs.description:
PhD Project in quantum and nonlinear light–matter interactions in plasmonic nanocavities

  The Niels Bohr Institute
 Faculty of SCIENCE

  University of Copenhagen

  The Niels Bohr Institute invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in experimental quantum nanophotonics. The project will be part of the newly established Mikkelsen Photonics group (Quantum, nonlinear and nanoscale light–matter interactions), funded by a Novo Nordisk Foundation RECRUIT grant.

  Start date is (expected to be) 15 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project

  Plasmonic nanocavities confine light to volumes thousands of times below the diffraction limit. In such extreme gaps, emission rates are enhanced by orders of magnitude, strong field gradients appear, and the usual rules of light–matter interaction are rewritten. The project builds on a wafer-scale platform developed in the group, in which colloidal quantum emitters (quantum dots or nanoplatelets) are deterministically placed into thousands of lithographically defined nanocavities with a controlled number of emitters per cavity. The PhD student will develop this platform and use it to study one or more of the following:

   	
• Few-emitter quantum optics: single-photon emission, collective emission, energy transfer and strong coupling with one to a few emitters per cavity. 	
• Cavity-enhanced nonlinear optics: using the extreme field confinement and field gradients of the nanogap to enhance and control nonlinear processes. 	
• Active and electrically tunable nanocavities: integrating functional materials (e.g. ferroelectric or two-dimensional materials) into the gap to switch and tune the emitter–cavity interaction.   The work is primarily experimental and involves nanofabrication, optical spectroscopy (photoluminescence, single-photon and photon-correlation measurements, nonlinear spectroscopy), optoelectronic device characterization and electromagnetic simulations. The specific project will be defined together with the successful candidate.

  Who are we looking for?

  We are looking for candidates within the fields of electrical engineering, physics, nanoscience, photonics, materials science or related areas. Applicants can have a background from optoelectronic or nanophotonic devices, semiconductor nanomaterials, optical spectroscopy, nanofabrication or electromagnetic simulation, but we will also consider candidates with different backgrounds. Hands-on experience with optical experiments and an interest in building new experimental setups is an advantage.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?

  The Mikkelsen Photonics group was established at the Niels Bohr Institute in 2026, when Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen moved from Duke University (USA) supported by a Novo Nordisk Foundation RECRUIT grant. The group studies quantum, nonlinear and nanoscale light–matter interactions in plasmonic nanocavities and is building a new laboratory combining deeply subwavelength cavities, single-photon spectroscopy, femtosecond pump–probe spectroscopy and, in a later phase, cryogenic and high-magnetic-field operation. As one of the first members of the group, the PhD student will have a central role in shaping the experiments and the scientific direction, with close supervision. The group is part of the Quantum Optics and Photonics research area at the Niels Bohr Institute, home to the Center for Hybrid Quantum Networks (Hy-Q), and has access to the nanofabrication facilities at the Niels Bohr Institute and the DTU Nanolab cleanroom.

  The group is a part of the Niels Bohr Institute, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen, in the new laboratory and office building of the Niels Bohr Institute.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and new, dedicated optics and nanofabrication facilities.

  Principal supervisor is Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen, The Niels Bohr Institute, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree.

  ************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Electrical Engineering, Physics, Nanoscience, Photonics or Materials Science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor’s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Physics.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year.

  A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.

  When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.
